metrics.label: Worldwide net sales and revenues
metrics.method: I start with the same-quarter reported consolidated base, FY2025 Q3 worldwide net sales and revenues of $12,018m. A segment/cycle angle is modestly positive for the consolidated line: PPA remains in a shipment-volume downturn (Q2 PPA sales -14% year on year), but Q2 Small Ag & Turf sales were +16% and Construction & Forestry +29%; applying a roughly 5% PPA decline against the FY2025 Q3 PPA sales base and continuing, but moderating, non-PPA growth produces approximately $12.8bn-$13.0bn. A seasonal-shape angle takes FY2026 Q2 reported total of $13,369m times FY2025 Q3/Q2 seasonal ratio of 12,018/12,763 = 94.2%, producing $12,589m; that understates the non-PPA momentum visible in FY2026 Q2, so I do not mechanically use it. The direct year-on-year angle, $12,018m x 1.069 = $12,847m, is selected and rounded to $12,850m. It gives material weight to PPA's continuing volume pressure and production discipline, but allows SAT/C&F growth, favorable currency and finance/other income to offset it. There is no quarterly consolidated-sales guide; the annual PPA sales guide (-5% to -10%) is a constraint rather than a direct quarterly forecast. This follows the required same-quarter seasonal/cycle approach rather than extrapolating the Q1-to-Q2 increase.
assumptions: PPA Q3 net sales decline about 5% year over year, less severe than Q2's 14% decline as dealer inventories normalize but still consistent with full-year PPA guidance of down 5%-10%.
SAT and C&F retain enough shipment/FX momentum to more than offset the PPA dollar decline, though their Q2 growth rates of 16% and 29% moderate in Q3.
No material change in FX, acquisition/disposal, or reporting basis occurs versus the May outlook.
drivers_applied: PPA lower shipment volumes and weak farmer sentiment
Dealer inventory normalization and aging fleet support

metrics.label: Diluted EPS (GAAP)
metrics.method: The same-quarter GAAP EPS base is FY2025 Q3 $4.75. The annual-guidance angle is the strongest available company forecast: FY2026 net income guidance midpoint is $4.75bn; reported FY2026 H1 net income implied by Q1 and Q2 GAAP EPS is approximately $0.656bn + $1.773bn = $2.429bn, leaving roughly $2.321bn for H2. With FY2025 Q3/Q4 net income of $1.289bn and $1.065bn, respectively, allocating the guided H2 remainder in that historical 54.8%/45.2% seasonal proportion gives Q3 net income of about $1.272bn; divided by approximately 271m diluted shares gives $4.69. A profitability/cost angle starts at $4.75 and subtracts continuing tariffs/higher production costs and lower PPA volume, partly offset by stronger SAT/C&F and modest price/FX, giving about $4.5-$4.7. I select $4.60, slightly below the annual-guide allocation because Q2 included the non-recurring $272m tariff recovery and Q3 continues to bear direct tariff costs. This is GAAP diluted EPS, not an adjusted figure, and respects the full-year guide while retaining uncertainty around H2 timing.
assumptions: Diluted weighted-average shares remain near Q2's 270.8m; $4.60 therefore corresponds to approximately $1.25bn of Q3 GAAP net income.
FY2026 full-year attributable net income lands near the $4.75bn guidance midpoint, rather than its $4.5bn or $5.0bn endpoints.
The Q2 $272m tariff-refund recovery does not recur in Q3, while a meaningful portion of the stated approximately $1.2bn FY2026 direct tariff exposure remains in cost of sales.

There is no conflict from news because it retrieved no verified items. The favorable Q2 margin print conflicts with persistent tariff costs, resolved by treating the documented tariff refund as one-time rather than carrying Q2 profitability into Q3.

metrics.label: Production & Precision Ag operating profit
metrics.method: The direct same-quarter base is FY2025 Q3 PPA operating profit of $580m on PPA sales of $4,273m, a 13.6% implied margin. A sales-and-guidance build assumes Q3 PPA sales of roughly $4.06bn (FY2025 Q3 $4.273bn x 95%), then applies a 12.3% operating margin, within management's FY2026 11%-13% full-year range: $4,060m x 12.3% = $499m, rounded to $500m. A prior-period angle is less helpful but corroborative: Q2 reported profit was $706m, including about $54m of the $272m refund allocated to PPA; removing that tailwind gives about $652m before recognizing Q3's normal seasonal mix and continuing lower volumes. The Q2 reported margin was 15.7%, but its non-recurring refund and Q2 seasonal strength pull it above the annual guided band, so I weight the explicit full-year margin guide rather than that spot margin. The historical cyclicality angle supports a lower profit than FY2025 Q3: PPA profit declined 50% in FY2025 Q3 as sales declined 16%, demonstrating adverse operating leverage; dealer inventories are healthier and price/FX help, so I forecast a much smaller 13.8% year-on-year profit decline rather than repeat that collapse. This explicitly treats volume/cost pressure as cyclical and the tariff refund as a one-off, not structural Q3 margin.
assumptions: PPA Q3 net sales are approximately $4,060m, or 5% below FY2025 Q3's $4,273m, consistent with the favorable-currency-inclusive FY2026 sales outlook of down 5%-10%.

Q3 PPA operating margin is 12.3%, inside management's 11%-13% full-year guidance and below FY2025 Q3's implied 13.6% because volume/mix and production costs outweigh about one point of price realization.
No further tariff-refund recovery is recognized; the Q2 recovery allocated 20% to PPA is excluded from Q3 profit.
drivers_applied: Price realization of roughly one point

forecast.reconciliation: The filings analyst is the primary source for all scored bases, same-quarter comparables, segment guidance, drivers, and accounting treatment. The financials analyst is used only as a shape/tie-out check for GAAP EPS and to reject its differently defined revenue line; it cannot support PPA segment profit. The news analyst retrieved no verified post-freeze development, so it supplies a currency limitation rather than a numerical adjustment. I prioritize same-quarter FY2025 reported results, then the latest FY2026 annual guidance, and explicitly remove the Q2 one-time tariff-refund benefit from forward margins.
forecast.sanity_checks: Worldwide net sales and revenues: $12,850m is +$832m / +6.9% versus FY2025 Q3 $12,018m; this is plausible because PPA weakness is offset by continuing SAT/C&F growth and FX, not because the ag cycle is assumed recovered. It is USD 12,850 million, i.e. USD 12.85 billion, not USD 12.850 million or USD 12.85m. It is inside the required 5,000-25,000 USDm band. Diluted EPS (GAAP): $4.60 is -$0.15 / -3.2% versus FY2025 Q3 $4.75; modest earnings pressure is plausible despite sales growth because tariffs, PPA mix and the absence of the Q2 refund weigh on margin. It is USD 4.60 per diluted share, not 4.60 cents and not an adjusted EPS figure. It is inside the required -5 to 20 USD/share band. Production & Precision Ag operating profit: $500m is -$80m / -13.8% versus FY2025 Q3 $580m; profit declines more than assumed sales because of volume/mix and production-cost operating leverage, moderated by inventory normalization, price and FX. It is USD 500 million of segment operating profit, i.e. USD 0.50 billion, not group operating income or PPA sales. It is inside the required -500 to 4,000 USDm band.
forecast.known_weaknesses: There is no direct quarterly company guidance for worldwide net sales, GAAP EPS, or Q3 PPA profit; Deere's closest guidance is annual net income and full-year PPA sales/margin. The news report is empty because all permitted searches failed, so no post-freeze crop, dealer, peer, tariff, FX, or order-book check was available. The financial-statement table has only five quarters, uses an ambiguous revenue definition below the scored worldwide total, and has no segment data. The largest forecast risk is Q3 shipment timing/dealer production discipline, followed by tariff accounting and whether the Q2 SAT/C&F strength persists. A verified change to FY2026 guidance, Q3 order/bookings commentary, or an additional tariff recovery would change these estimates.
